topic: OP FY2027 budget and proposed budget reduction
summary: The chair presented the Office of the President's proposed FY2027 allocation as 10,156,000,000, while Executive Secretary Ralph Recto stated a proposal of MXN 10,150,000,000. Recto said the proposal was about 0.14% of the proposed national budget and was 64% lower than the previous year's level because of reduced operational requirements and the completion of ASEAN Summit activities. He said the amount would support the Office of the President's 49 delivery units and core presidential operations. The minority and majority moved to extend institutional and interbranch courtesy and terminate the committee deliberations. A minority member objected and raised transparency, flood-control, and confidential and intelligence fund questions, including 550,000,000 in such funds. The motion passed with 37 votes in favor and five against, while the chair recorded that outstanding questions would be answered on or before plenary.
question: What was the Office of the President's proposed FY2027 allocation, and why was it reportedly lower than the previous year's level? The committee also sought to determine whether questions on flood control and confidential and intelligence funds would receive answers despite terminating the committee-level deliberations.
agency_position: The Office of the President said its proposed FY2027 budget was sufficient to perform its constitutional and administrative functions. Executive Secretary Ralph Recto attributed the reduction to lower operational requirements and the completion of ASEAN Summit-related activities, and said the agency was ready to answer questions.
outcome: The committee granted institutional and interbranch courtesy and terminated the Office of the President's committee-level budget deliberations by a vote of 37-5. Questions on flood control and confidential and intelligence funds remained for answers on or before plenary.

topic: Confidential and intelligence funds and spending transparency
summary: Members objected to ending the Office of the President budget discussion without scrutiny of confidential and intelligence funds and related accountability issues. One member cited 550,000,000 in confidential and intelligence funds, while other members raised transparency, flood-control, and possible political-patronage concerns. The Office of the President did not give a substantive answer in these stretches, although Executive Secretary Ralph Recto stated that the office respected Congress's authority and was ready to answer questions. Rep. Edgar Erice supported the budget and said confidential funds were necessary, while Rep. Iris Marie Montes said her negative vote defended Congress's duty to scrutinize every peso of public funds. The chair carried the motion to terminate deliberations by a vote of 37 to five and committed the outstanding answers to the plenary stage.
question: The committee was trying to establish whether the Office of the President's confidential and intelligence funds, and related budgetary issues, would receive meaningful congressional scrutiny and transparent accountability before approval. It also sought to determine when the Office of the President would answer the questions deferred by the committee's grant of institutional and interbranch courtesy.
agency_position: The Office of the President stated that it respected Congress's constitutional authority and was ready to answer questions. It did not provide a substantive answer in the cited stretches on the transparency, accountability, or use of confidential and intelligence funds; the chair recorded that responses would be provided on or before plenary.
outcome: The committee granted institutional and interbranch courtesy and terminated the Office of the President budget deliberations, but members' transparency and confidential-fund questions remained unanswered. The chair recorded the Office of the President's responses as due on or before plenary.

summary: Rep. Edgar Erice raised flood-control anomalies while discussing the President's budget, fiscal space, and developmental spending. Rep. Rufus Rodriguez supported the Office of the President budget and said the flood-control projects in the 2nd District of Cagayan de Oro were completed, compliant, and cleared by COA, NBI, DPWH, and NEDA. He also said persons responsible for irregularities should face justice through the Ombudsman. A separate member said plenary answers remained due and raised questions about flood control, possible kickbacks, and the transparency of confidential and intelligence funds. The member cited 550 million in confidential and intelligence funds, while other budget figures raised during the related discussion included about 58 billion in presidential pork and about 1.1 trillion for developmental projects. The excerpt ended without an agency response, leaving the questions parked for plenary.
question: The committee was seeking to establish how flood-control anomalies and alleged irregularities related to the Office of the President budget and executive oversight. Members also sought clarification on alleged kickbacks, the role of executive officials, and the reported use of confidential and intelligence funds.
agency_position: No agency official provided a substantive answer on flood-control anomalies, alleged kickbacks, or the use of confidential and intelligence funds in the excerpt. The only position presented in support of the Office of the President was from Rep. Rodriguez, who said his district had no ghost or substandard flood-control projects and that its projects had passed several agency examinations.
outcome: No agency answer was given on the alleged flood-control anomalies, possible kickbacks, or confidential-fund transparency questions. The matters were left for answers in plenary, while Rep. Rodriguez placed on record his defense of flood-control projects in his district.

topic: Developmental projects and available fiscal space
summary: Rep. Edgar Erice expressed support for the President's proposed budget while discussing austerity, economic deceleration, and the fiscal space available for developmental projects. He cited capital-outlay or developmental-project shares of about 25% in 2023, 21% in 2024, and 19% in both 2025 and 2026. He also mentioned presidential-pork figures of 58,000,000,000 and 8,000,000,000, scholarship funding of 100,000, and developmental projects of 1,100,000,000,000. Rep. Erice referenced 1,600,000,000 trillion and 1,600,000,000,000, with the first expression unclear, and raised absorptive capacity as a concern. No agency official answered, no document or funding commitment was made, and the chair treated the remarks as a significant manifestation before moving on.

outcome: The issue remained informational: Rep. Erice presented his support, concerns, and figures, but no agency response or specific fiscal-space determination was recorded. The chair accepted the manifestation and moved to the next participant.

thread.said: Rep. Erice, noting that he was not a member of the Appropriations Committee, expressed support for the President's 10,000,000,000 budget and linked it to austerity.

thread.speaker: Rep. Edgar Erice
thread.said: He warned of severe quarterly deceleration reflected in GDP and cited inflation and a flood-control budget anomaly as external or fiscal concerns. He also referenced Vietnamese GDP growth of 8%.

thread.speaker: Rep. Edgar Erice
thread.said: He compared fiscal space for developmental projects and capital outlays across years: 25% in 2023, 21% in 2024, and 19% in both 2025 and 2026.

thread.speaker: Rep. Edgar Erice
thread.said: Rep. Erice questioned the fiscal space available for developmental projects and referred to "1637% pork soft and hard pork" and presidential pork of 58,000,000,000. The wording and the 1637% figure were unclear in the transcript.

thread.speaker: Rep. Edgar Erice
thread.said: He cited presidential pork of 8,000,000,000, scholarship funding of 100,000, and the issue of absorptive capacity.

thread.speaker: Rep. Edgar Erice
thread.said: He referred to 1,600,000,000 trillion and separately stated 1,600,000,000,000. He then identified 1,100,000,000,000 for developmental projects.

thread.speaker: Rep. Edgar Erice
thread.said: He distinguished developmental projects from government operations and personnel services, stating that the cited development amount was not MOOE. He also referred to the economy at 410%.

thread.speaker: The chair
thread.said: The chair thanked Rep. Erice for his significant manifestation and proceeded to recognize the next participant.

summary: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez raised the President's assistance to farmers and fisherfolk while manifesting full support for the Office of the President's budget. He said the President had distributed 10,000 to farmers and fisherfolk in Region 10. He also cited congressional access to DSWD, DOLE, TESDA, and the Department of Health as related support. No agency official answered or contested the statement, and the chair accepted Rep. Rodriguez's manifestation.

outcome: The assistance was cited in support of the Office of the President's budget. No question was directed to the agency, and no additional action or clarification was recorded.

summary: Executive Secretary Ralph Recto raised the ASEAN Summit in presenting the OP's proposed FY 2027 budget. He said the proposed budget was 64% lower than the previous year's level, partly because activities related to the Philippines' hosting of the Summit had been completed. He stated that no additional funding would be required for the Summit in FY 2027. The agency treated the existing proposal as sufficient and did not identify a continuing Summit-related funding need. No member questioned the statement or requested supporting documents in the provided excerpt.
question: The committee was being informed how the completion of activities related to the Philippines' hosting of the ASEAN Summit affected the Office of the President's proposed FY 2027 budget. The presentation also established whether the OP expected to seek additional ASEAN Summit funding in FY 2027.
agency_position: The Office of the President said that activities related to the Philippines' hosting of the ASEAN Summit had been completed and that no additional funding would be required for them in FY 2027. It attributed part of the lower proposed budget to that completion.
outcome: The OP's presentation established that it did not seek additional FY 2027 funding for the ASEAN Summit because the related hosting activities had been completed. No committee challenge, document request, or separate funding action was recorded in the excerpt.

topic: Commission on Audit opinion and budget accountability
summary: Executive Secretary Ralph Recto raised fiscal discipline and accountability as central principles in the Office of the President's operations. He reported that COA had issued the OP an unmodified opinion for fiscal year 2025, described as the highest audit opinion an agency may receive. He said it was the OP's third consecutive unmodified opinion since 2022 and meant that its financial statements were fairly presented and compliant with applicable public sector accounting standards. Recto characterized the opinion as a badge of good housekeeping and evidence that public funds were accounted for. He also stated that the proposed budget followed DBM parameters and sought no special treatment. The issue remained informational, with no recorded committee follow-up or unresolved challenge.
question: The committee was assessing whether the Office of the President had maintained proper financial management and accountability for public funds. The presentation focused on the significance of the Commission on Audit opinion and its relevance to the proposed budget.
agency_position: The Office of the President presented its unmodified COA opinion as evidence of sound financial management, accurate financial reporting, and accountability for public funds. It maintained that the proposed budget was prepared under standard DBM rules without seeking special treatment.
outcome: The agency presented the unmodified COA opinion and its implications for financial accountability. No committee challenge, document request, or further action on the audit opinion was recorded in the provided stretch.
